newsitem.title: TAIWAN: GOLF-ELS MAKES PROMISING START TO ASIAN MARATHON.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS MAKES PROMISING START TO ASIAN MARATHON.

text.p: South Africa's Ernie Els birdied the last three holes to shoot a five-under-par 67 and earn a share of the first round lead in the Johnnie Walker Super Tour with Lin Keng-chi of Taiwan and Korea's Park Nam-sin on Tuesday.

The eight-man event, being staged in four different Asian countries over six days, also features Europe's top two players, Scotland's Colin Montgomerie and Ian Woosnam of Wales, who were a stroke behind after opening 68s in unseasonably hot conditions at the Ta Shee Golf & Country Club.
Felix Casas of the Philippines shot a nine-under-par 71, a stroke better than Fiji's Vijay Singh who had a poor day on the greens.

The youngest player in the field, Thailand's Chawalit Plaphol who is in his rookie year on the Asian PGA Tour, shot a two-over-par 74 but signed for a 75 which he was credited with under tournament rules.

The entire field now flies to Korea on Wednesday and play the second round at the Seoul Country Club on Thursday. The third round is at the Orchard Golf & Country Club in Manila on Friday with the final round at Thana City Golf & Country Club in Bangkok on Sunday.

Three-time World Matchplay champion Els said he was delighted to have prevented the Asians opening up a lead. "The overseas players will have to play well, these (Asian) boys mean business," he said. "I'm delighted with a 67. I had a really excellent local caddy and she helped me get the score."
Montgomerie recovered from an indifferent start to shoot four birdies in the back nine for a 68.
"I suffered quite a lot in the heat. The greens were pretty tricky for the overseas players," said the four-time European Order of Merit winner.
